title: Pixel Metropolis : Antiquity Early Preview
author: Odd_Revolution7522
selftext:
Can't believe its already been 3 months since I opened Codex for the first time and started working on my historical city builder.

I wanted to do an update of where development of the game is as Next Fest begins.

I've kept working on Antiquity in parallel of the demo build, it's taken more time than I thought, not necessarily because Codex struggles with the codebase, but more because adding one system cascades into new mechanics and tweaks.

The missing part from my AI workflow was composite sprites : buildings that handle z-indexing and ambient citizens inside without breaking the isometric illusion. The market is the first building in the game that leverages it fully, with citizens going around the building without stepping over stalls and roofs.

There is still about a month of work before I can confidently release in Early Access with the four first eras out of seven (Paleolithic, Neolithic, Metal Age, Antiquity, Medieval, Industrial, Modern).

IMO the big differentiator of AI is how easy it is to produce visually rich worlds with tons of building variations and props that have weathered and ruined states as time goes by.

If you want to see what a full AI workflow can build over time, feel free to check the free demo on Steam !

[https://store.steampowered.com/app/5166960/Pixel\_Metropolis/](https://store.steampowered.com/app/5166960/Pixel_Metropolis/)

comments.author: castor44_
comments.body:
How did you create the pixel art assets? Or are they ready-made? 

Because I’ve noticed that AI isn’t very good at pixel art at the moment, so I’ve actually even started doing it by hand myself :D

replies.author: Odd_Revolution7522
replies.body:
They are all generated with Codex’s native imagegen.

I find it pretty good actually after you implement design systems and scaffolds around the generation.

But yes what you see is often not the first version of the building, I reject a lot of results along the way.

comments.author: RedHood31
comments.body: Why it's not web browser based anymore :( I really liked the easy way to access it

replies.author: Odd_Revolution7522
replies.body:
For two main reasons :   
\- As I add more features and buildings the Chrome build starts to reach its limits, a standalone executive gives me more room for performance improvements.  
\- I really don't want to handle cross saves, payment processing, refunds etc myself. Steam does all of this for me, so I can concentrate on the actual game.

The demo will stay on the website though.
